key_insight: Finite homotopy linearisation yields a nilpotent generator whose polynomial evolution enables direct quantum simulation of approximate compressible flow without time-stepping error.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a quantum-circuit route to non-isothermal compressible Navier–Stokes simulation, with energy-budget diagnostics defining observable-specific accuracy windows.
method: Form polynomial residuals in primitive variables and apply periodic-grid stencils consistently across shifted products.
Lift the finite homotopy hierarchy into a strictly block lower-triangular linear system.
Compile finite-polynomial evolution into logical quantum circuits and extract a signed velocity Fourier mode through Hadamard interference.
evidence_signal: Two-dimensional Taylor–Green tests at Mach 0.2 and 0.4 show fifth-order accuracy lasting longer for viscous dissipation than pressure-dilatation at equal relative tolerance; coarse-grid circuits verify signed readout and measure gate counts.
watch_item: Removing time-stepping error does not remove homotopy truncation or spatial discretisation error, and finer-grid circuit normalisation costs remain an implementation concern.
paper_title: Direct quantum simulation of compressible Navier-Stokes flow via finite homotopy linearisation
